narrative.overview:
This portfolio reads as a bright, personal shoreline: a fixed photographic backdrop (warm sky and water), deep harbor ink for type, and sky-blue accents that mark navigation and interaction without shouting. Density stays comfortable for a single-page scroll plus a dedicated contact route; nothing competes with the hero name and section headlines. Cards and pills feel light and approachable, appropriate for a student developer presenting work and studies, not a SaaS product.

The system rejects dark-mode neon, purple gradients, generic AI tool marketing chrome, and template landing-page rhythms (metric heroes, identical icon grids, decorative glass everywhere). Depth comes from hover lift and soft shadows, not from stacked modal layers or heavy chrome.
keyCharacteristics: Light, photographic canvas with transparent or low-opacity surfaces
Deep Harbor Ink (#0a2342) as the single authoritative text and outline color
Skyline Mist (#93c5fd) for borders, rings, and outline-button fills on hover
Pill-shaped CTAs and tags; gently rounded cards (8px)
System sans stack only; hierarchy via size and weight, not display serifs
Motion: short ease-out transitions, vertical lift on hover, one hero entrance animation
Italian copy; section anchors with generous scroll-mt for the fixed header

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Harbor Ink is the only dark hue for brand text and outlines. Do not introduce second navies, charcoals, or pure black for headings.

rules.name: The Mist Border Rule
rules.body: Structural borders use Skyline Mist (border-blue-300). Heavier borders (blue-900) appear only for WIP or emphasis states, not as default card chrome.

rules.name: The Light Headline Rule
rules.body: Section titles use font-light at very large sizes; card titles use font-bold at modest sizes. Never bold a section title to match a card.

rules.name: The System-Only Rule
rules.body: No webfont imports until explicitly chosen; new screens inherit the system stack.

rules.name: The Lift-on-Hover Rule
rules.body: Interactive cards lift vertically (-translate-y-1) and deepen shadow on hover. At rest they stay visually light on the photo background.

rules.name: The No-Modal-First Rule
rules.body: Mobile navigation uses a slide-over drawer (Headless UI), not centered modals. New flows should prefer inline panels or dedicated routes (like /contact).

dos: Do keep the fixed photographic background (background4.png, background-attachment: fixed) as the canvas; place content in transparent or lightly bordered layers on top.
Do use Harbor Ink for all primary text and outline buttons; use Slate Body only for supporting copy.
Do use Skyline Mist borders to tie sections together (footer rules, cards, inputs).
Do apply hover lift (-translate-y-1) + shadow deepen on interactive cards.
Do use pill shapes for CTAs and tags; reserve rounded-lg for form controls and large panels.
Do keep motion between 100ms and 300ms with ease-out or ease-in-out; hero entrance uses the fade-in-slide-up keyframe (900ms, slide from left).
Do maintain scroll-mt-28 (or equivalent) on anchored sections for the fixed header.
Do write UI copy in Italian for this site.
donts: Don't ship AI slop / template SaaS patterns: gradient text, identical card grids (icon + title + repeated blurb), decorative glassmorphism, or the hero-metric cliché.
Don't look like a portfolio bootcamp generico: copied layout, stock-icon filler, zero personal voice.
Don't go troppo giocoso o caotico: random colors, excessive animation, or infantilism that undermines professional credibility.
Don't chase empty moderno e pulito; every expressive choice needs a reason (personalità con disciplina).
Don't use pure #000 or #fff for text or surfaces; tint toward Harbor Ink or warm off-whites.
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe on cards or alerts.
Don't spread backdrop-blur beyond the fixed header and mobile overlay backdrop.
Don't default to centered modals for navigation or forms; use routes (/contact) or slide-overs.
Don't introduce em dashes in UX copy; use commas, colons, or periods.
Don't add display serifs or monospace stacks without updating this file and the frontmatter typography block.
